findings.location: Increment A, step 4; Goal and completion criterion 1
findings.problem: The watchdog is started only after the launcher. If the engine is killed in the interval after `Popen` creates the launcher and before the watchdog is ready, no independent process knows the launcher's group ID, so the launcher can outlive the engine. The proposed SIGKILL test kills a driver once the call is running and does not force this startup window, so it cannot establish the stated “any way” guarantee.
findings.suggestion: Redesign the startup handoff so supervision exists before a launcher can run—for example, have an independent wrapper/watchdog create and own the launcher—or narrow the guarantee explicitly. Add a deterministic test that interrupts the startup handoff at the relevant boundary.

summary: The plan has an unaddressed launcher-before-watchdog race that defeats its core guarantee.
